details:
What ARES Does

ARES (Advanced Reconnaissance & Exploration System) is a web-based planetary terrain intelligence platform designed to explore and analyze the surface of Mars using real NASA HiRISE Digital Terrain Model data from the Gale Crater region.

The system reconstructs the study area as an interactive 3D terrain environment. Users can rotate, zoom, and examine the landscape through four visualization layers: Elevation, Hillshade, Slope, and Hazard Classification.

How It Works

ARES processes the elevation model into terrain visualization assets and derives slope measurements for scientific analysis. Its hazard engine classifies valid terrain pixels into four categories: Gentle (below 5°), Moderate (5°–15°), Steep (15°–25°), and Very Steep (25° or greater).

The terrain inspection feature allows users to select locations and retrieve elevation, slope, geographic coordinates, and raster pixel information.

ARES also implements an A* pathfinding algorithm for experimental terrain-aware rover route planning. Users select start and destination points on the 3D terrain. The algorithm searches a slope-based planning grid while excluding NoData and very steep terrain. Each generated route includes distance, average and maximum slope, a waypoint slope profile, and a mission assessment.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ARES brings planetary terrain visualization, quantitative hazard screening, and route planning into one interactive platform. It helps users understand the relationship between surface topography and potential rover navigation constraints.

The project demonstrates how open planetary datasets and computational methods can be combined to support exploration research, scientific learning, and future development of terrain-aware robotic planning tools.

Technology Stack

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, HTML, CSS
  • 3D visualization: Three.js, React Three Fiber, React Three Drei
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI
  • Scientific processing: Rasterio, GDAL, NumPy
  • Communication: Axios and REST APIs
  • Algorithms: A* pathfinding and slope-based terrain classification

Creativity and Innovation

ARES connects actual planetary elevation measurements to an interactive 3D environment and an experimental rover route-planning workflow. Rather than presenting terrain as a static image, it allows users to inspect individual locations, compare scientific layers, analyze terrain hazards, and generate routes based on measurable terrain constraints.

Limitations

The route planner uses a downsampled 256 × 544 planning grid and slope-based screening. Its results are experimental and have not been validated for actual rover mobility or mission safety. Hazard classification is preliminary terrain screening, not a certified safety assessment.
